findings.evidence: The file has a fully written '## Review' section describing the code-review findings, and then ends with a second '## Review\n\n(filled after implementation)' — an unremoved template placeholder that now contradicts/duplicates the section above it.

findings.summary: Line-number citation for isCheckboxChecked is slightly off from the actual function definition (points into its docstring rather than the function signature).
findings.evidence: Doc says '`isCheckboxChecked` (`data-validation.ts:149`)' — line 149 in the current file falls inside the function's docstring comment; the actual `export function isCheckboxChecked` signature is at line 158. Minor imprecision, not a substantive contradiction.

findings.summary: Formula read-only guard misses spill ghost cells: toggle still reports `true` while `setData` silently no-ops
findings.evidence: The new guard is `if (cell?.f) return false;` (sheet.ts:3842). A checkbox placed over a *spilled* formula result is a ghost cell: it carries `spillAnchor` and `v` but no `f`, so the guard does not fire. Execution reaches `await this.setData(ref, next)` (sheet.ts:3846), but `setData` bails at line 1004 (`if (existing?.spillAnchor) return;`) — nothing is written, yet `toggleCheckboxAt` returns `true`. Callers treat `true` as "a toggle happened" (view/worksheet.ts:4853 re-renders; view/spreadsheet.ts:365 re-renders and notifies), so the UI reports a state change that never occurred. The same 'the formula drives the state' rationale in the new comment applies to ghost cells, and the guard should cover `cell?.spillAnchor` too (or the return value should reflect whether the write actually landed).

findings.summary: Case-fold branch gated on strict `=== undefined`, so a rule deserialized with `checkedValue: null` loses case-insensitive matching
findings.evidence: `if (rule.checkedValue === undefined && rule.uncheckedValue === undefined)` (data-validation.ts:163) uses strict `undefined`, while the sibling helpers `checkedValueOf`/`uncheckedValueOf` (lines 140/143) use `??`, i.e. they treat `null` as 'not set'. A rule that round-trips through JSON/CRDT storage with an explicit `null` for these optional fields therefore takes the exact-match path even though it is semantically a default boolean checkbox, so a lowercase `"true"` from xlsx import renders unchecked — the exact case the change is meant to fix. Using the same `?? undefined`/nullish test in both places would make the two consistent.

findings.summary: Formula-cell guard test never asserts that no literal value was written, despite claiming it
findings.evidence: The test comment at line 66 says "reports false, keeps the formula, writes no literal" and the task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260712-checkbox-validation-bugfix-todo.md:35) specifies "leaves cell.f intact, writes no v", but the only post-toggle assertion is `expect(cell?.f).toBe('=1=1')` (line 69). `cell?.v` (the formula-computed 'TRUE') is never asserted, so a regression that kept `f` but clobbered/stale-wrote `v` would pass. The test is still discriminating for the guard itself (without the guard `setData(ref,'FALSE')` clears `f`), so this is a strengthening gap, not fake coverage.

findings.summary: No test for a rule with only a custom checkedValue (uncheckedValue undefined) — half of the new `&&` gate is unexercised
findings.evidence: The new gate is `rule.checkedValue === undefined && rule.uncheckedValue === undefined` (data-validation.ts:163). Tests cover both-custom-set (lines 107-116) and uncheckedValue-only (lines 118-128), but never checkedValue-only. Mutating the gate to `rule.uncheckedValue === undefined` alone would still pass every test in the file, so that operand of the conjunction has no independent coverage (e.g. `{checkedValue:'true'}` with value 'TRUE' should be false).

mergedFrom.summary: toggleCheckboxValue not tested against a custom-value rule with a non-canonical input
mergedFrom.evidence: Only `toggleCheckboxValue(rule,'true') === CHECKBOX_FALSE` on a default rule is asserted (line 104). The doc claims toggle 'inherits the fix by delegation'; no test pins that a custom-value rule ('Yes'/'No') toggles 'yes' → 'Yes' (i.e. remains exact-match through the toggle path).

findings.summary: Formula guard returns the same `false` as "no checkbox rule here", so callers cannot distinguish read-only-formula from not-a-checkbox
findings.evidence: `toggleCheckboxAt` now returns `false` both when no checkbox rule resolves and when the cell is formula-backed. The click path (`worksheet.ts:3405`) and Space path (`worksheet.ts:4853`) therefore cannot give the user any feedback (no flash/toast/tooltip) that the checkbox is intentionally read-only — a click on the glyph simply appears to do nothing. The task doc calls this out as "design intent: formula-backed checkbox is read-only (GS parity)", and Google Sheets does render/behave distinguishably. A distinct return (or a `getCheckboxToggleState`) would keep the API honest. Taste/API-shape preference, non-blocking.

findings.summary: Implementation is stricter than the stated fix scope (gated on both custom values absent, not just `checkedValue`)
findings.evidence: The originating task (`docs/tasks/active/20260712-checkbox-validation-bugfix-todo.md:25`) scopes the fix to "default boolean checkbox only (no custom `checkedValue`)". The code requires BOTH `checkedValue` and `uncheckedValue` to be undefined. This deviation is deliberate and better (it avoids inverting a custom `uncheckedValue: "true"`), and is documented in the doc comment and the task Review section, but the task's Plan bullet (line 32-33) still states the narrower rule, so the spec text and code disagree. Worth aligning the task/design wording.

findings.summary: Task doc has two `## Review` sections, the second still an unfilled placeholder

findings.summary: No paired `*-lessons.md` for the task, and the all-[x] todo is still in `docs/tasks/active/`
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:54-55 requires paired `YYYYMMDD-<slug>-todo.md` / `-lessons.md` files, and CLAUDE.md:64 archives completed tasks via `pnpm tasks:archive`. Every checkbox in the todo is `[x]` yet it remains under `docs/tasks/active/` with no lessons file. This is normally done at merge time, so it is a nit, not a blocker.

findings.summary: Unbounded `value.toUpperCase()` on document-controlled cell content in the per-repaint render path (availability hardening)
findings.evidence: `isCheckboxChecked` now falls back to `value.toUpperCase() === CHECKBOX_TRUE` (data-validation.ts:166). Its only non-test caller on the hot path is `GridCanvas.renderCellCheckbox` (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1042), which runs for every visible checkbox-ruled cell on every repaint. `value` is `cell.v` — arbitrary-length content that a collaborator (Yorkie sync), an xlsx import, or a paste can set; I found no cell-value length cap in packages/sheets (grepped MaxCell*/maxLength/truncat*). Vector: a peer writes a multi-megabyte string into a cell covered by a default checkbox rule; because a checkbox cell renders a glyph instead of its text, this comparison becomes the only per-frame work touching that string, and it now allocates a full uppercase copy per frame (previously `value === 'TRUE'` short-circuited on length), causing GC churn / scroll freeze for anyone viewing that region. Mitigation: bail out when `value.length !== CHECKBOX_TRUE.length` before case-folding. I did not measure the freeze, hence medium confidence.

findings.summary: Rule-supplied `checkedValue`/`uncheckedValue` is written through `setData`, which turns a leading `=` into a formula; the rule fields are never validated
findings.evidence: `toggleCheckboxValue` returns `rule.checkedValue` verbatim (data-validation.ts:180) and `Sheet.toggleCheckboxAt` feeds it to `setData` (sheet.ts:3846). `setData` -> `inferInput` treats any value starting with `=` as a formula (input.ts:234, sheet.ts:1033-1034), and `normalizeDataValidationRule` (data-validation.ts:66-102) validates only id/kind/ranges/list/date operands — `checkedValue`/`uncheckedValue` are copied unchecked and unbounded. Vector: a malicious collaborator or a crafted import installs a checkbox rule with `checkedValue: '=HYPERLINK("…","OK")'` (HYPERLINK exists: functions-lookup.ts:869); the next victim click on that checkbox plants the attacker's formula into the victim's own cell — a stored formula-injection primitive driven by rule metadata rather than cell content. The newly added `cell?.f` guard (sheet.ts:3842) prevents overwriting an existing formula but does not prevent creating one. Pre-existing rather than introduced here, and the injector already has cell-write rights in the collaborative model, so privilege gain is limited — hence low confidence. Mitigation: reject/normalize checkbox custom values that begin with `=` (or write them as literals).
searchedFor: Grep 'checkedValue|uncheckedValue' repo-wide (only types.ts, data-validation.ts, tests, docs — no importer or validator sets/validates them)
Read Sheet.setData / inferInput to confirm leading '=' becomes cell.f
Grep 'IMPORTDATA|WEBSERVICE|IMPORTXML|HYPERLINK' in packages/sheets/src for a payload sink

findings.evidence: The added task file records a prior review outcome and states a finding "was dismissed by the verifier" (line 52) plus CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE verdict labels. It contains no instruction aimed at a reviewer and reads as a legitimate work log, so I treated it as data and reviewed the code independently; noting it only because such text can pre-empt a later reviewer's finding. No action required beyond awareness.

findings.summary: New formula read-only guard checks only `cell?.f`, so spill-ghost cells (array-formula results) still reach `setData` and `toggleCheckboxAt` reports `true` for a write that silently never happens
findings.evidence: Guard added at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3842 tests only `cell.f`. A cell that is a spill ghost of an array formula carries `spillAnchor` + `v` but no `f` (see the ghost-cell contract at sheet.ts:1004: `if (existing?.spillAnchor) return;`). So a checkbox over a spilled formula result passes the new guard, calls `setData` (sheet.ts:3846), which returns early without writing, yet `toggleCheckboxAt` returns `true`. Callers that trust the return — packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:365-367 and packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4853 — re-render believing the state flipped, and the stated invariant "a formula drives the state, the control is read-only" is not enforced for array-formula-driven checkboxes. Fix belongs on the new guard (also check `cell?.spillAnchor`).

findings.summary: Space-key handler still matches and `preventDefault()`s over a formula-backed checkbox cell, so the key is now swallowed with no action and no feedback
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4844-4856: `match` only checks `kind === 'checkbox'` and `!this.readOnly`; `run` calls `event.preventDefault()` then `toggleCheckboxAt`, which after this change returns `false` for a formula cell. Previously Space toggled; now the keystroke is consumed and nothing happens (no read-only toast / no fall-through to normal Space handling). The caller was not updated for the new precondition.

findings.summary: Click-to-toggle path ignores `toggleCheckboxAt`'s return value, so a click on the glyph of a formula cell preventDefaults, forces a repaint and gives no indication the control is read-only
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:3402-3407 calls `await this.sheet!.toggleCheckboxAt(ref); this.render(); return;` unconditionally, discarding the boolean. With the new formula guard the call can now be a no-op, but the handler still consumes the click and repaints. Unlike the Space handler (worksheet.ts:4853) it does not branch on the result.

findings.summary: Case-folding branch is gated on strict `=== undefined`, so a rule whose `checkedValue`/`uncheckedValue` round-trips as `null` (CRDT/JSON/REST import — the very sources the change cites) silently loses the new case-insensitivity
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/data-validation.ts:163 uses `rule.checkedValue === undefined && rule.uncheckedValue === undefined`, while `checkedValueOf`/`uncheckedValueOf` (lines 140/143) use `??`, which treats `null` as absent. Rules are persisted and re-read through the Yorkie document (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:892-907) and `cloneDataValidationRule` spreads whatever fields exist, so a rule stored with an explicit `null` custom value would behave as a default checkbox for `checkedValueOf` but as a custom checkbox for the new branch. Confirming needs evidence that any writer (xlsx import / REST payload / CRDT serialization) can produce `null` rather than dropping the key.

+# Checkbox data-validation bug fixes
+
+Follow-ups from the data-validation design doc (`docs/design/sheets/data-validation.md`,
+Phase-1 "Not yet guarded" note). Two clear correctness bugs in the shipped
+checkbox control, each self-contained.
+
+## Bugs
+
+1. **Formula cell is not read-only under a checkbox rule.**
+   `Sheet.toggleCheckboxAt` (`sheet.ts:3834`) reads `cell?.v` and writes a
+   literal `TRUE`/`FALSE` via `setData` without checking `cell.f`. Toggling a
+   checkbox that sits over a formula cell **overwrites the formula**. Design
+   intent: a formula-backed checkbox is read-only (the formula drives the
+   state) — Google Sheets / Excel parity. Both the click path
+   (`worksheet.ts:3405`) and the Space path (`worksheet.ts:4853`) route through
+   `toggleCheckboxAt`, so one guard fixes both.
+
+2. **`isCheckboxChecked` is case-sensitive.**
+   `isCheckboxChecked` (`data-validation.ts:149`) compares `value === 'TRUE'`
+   exactly, so a cell holding `"true"` renders **unchecked**. `setData`
+   normalizes typed input to `"TRUE"`, but values arriving via xlsx import /
+   REST API / external paste can be lowercase and bypass normalization. The
+   formula engine (`formula.ts:1054`) and input parser (`input.ts:242`) already
+   treat `TRUE`/`FALSE` case-insensitively; the render/toggle path should match.
+   Fix scope: **default boolean checkbox only** (no custom `checkedValue`) —
+   a custom checked value stays an exact string match (GS parity).
+
+## Plan (TDD)
+
+- [x] Model test: `isCheckboxChecked` matches `"true"`/`"True"`/`"TRUE"` for a
+      default rule; a custom-value rule stays exact-match.
+- [x] Model fix: `isCheckboxChecked` case-insensitive for the fully-default
+      boolean checkbox only; `toggleCheckboxValue` inherits the fix (delegates).
+- [x] Sheet test: `toggleCheckboxAt` over a formula cell is a no-op — returns
+      `false`, leaves `cell.f` intact, writes no `v`.
+- [x] Sheet fix: guard `toggleCheckboxAt` on `cell?.f`.
+- [x] `pnpm test` (sheets) green; `pnpm verify:fast` green (EXIT 0).
+- [x] Update design doc Phase-1 "Not yet guarded" note (both now fixed).
+
+## Review
+
+High-effort workflow code review (`Workflow code-review`, 4 finders + verify)
+surfaced two findings, both addressed:
+
+- **[0] correctness (PLAUSIBLE)** — case-fold branch was gated only on
+  `checkedValue === undefined`, so a rule with a custom `uncheckedValue` that
+  upper-cases to `"TRUE"` inverted state. Fixed: case-folding now requires
+  *both* custom values absent; added a regression test.
+- **[1] cleanup (CONFIRMED)** — `value.toUpperCase()` allocated per repaint,
+  against the file's no-alloc convention. Fixed: canonical `TRUE`/`FALSE`
+  short-circuit before the `toUpperCase` fallback.
+
+A refuted finding ("silently depends on `CHECKBOX_TRUE` being uppercase") was
+dismissed by the verifier — `CHECKBOX_TRUE` is a module constant.
+
+Both bugs are model/Sheet-level; the click and Space view paths route through
+`toggleCheckboxAt` and the render path through `isCheckboxChecked`, so no
+view-layer change was needed. View-layer smoke deferred (Phase-1 precedent).
+
+## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)
+
+- Space range-uniform "set all checked" (parity feature, not a bug).
+- Merged-cell glyph/hit-test mismatch.
+- Eager `FALSE` materialization for `COUNTIF`.
+- Custom checkbox values UI.
+
+## Review
+
+(filled after implementation)

samples.summary: Unbounded `value.toUpperCase()` on document-controlled cell content in the per-repaint render path (availability hardening)
samples.evidence: `isCheckboxChecked` now falls back to `value.toUpperCase() === CHECKBOX_TRUE` (data-validation.ts:166). Its only non-test caller on the hot path is `GridCanvas.renderCellCheckbox` (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1042), which runs for every visible checkbox-ruled cell on every repaint. `value` is `cell.v` — arbitrary-length content that a collaborator (Yorkie sync), an xlsx import, or a paste can set; I found no cell-value length cap in packages/sheets (grepped MaxCell*/maxLength/truncat*). Vector: a peer writes a multi-megabyte string into a cell covered by a default checkbox rule; because a checkbox cell renders a glyph instead of its text, this comparison becomes the only per-frame work touching that string, and it now allocates a full uppercase copy per frame (previously `value === 'TRUE'` short-circuited on length), causing GC churn / scroll freeze for anyone viewing that region. Mitigation: bail out when `value.length !== CHECKBOX_TRUE.length` before case-folding. I did not measure the freeze, hence medium confidence.

samples.summary: Rule-supplied `checkedValue`/`uncheckedValue` is written through `setData`, which turns a leading `=` into a formula; the rule fields are never validated
samples.evidence: `toggleCheckboxValue` returns `rule.checkedValue` verbatim (data-validation.ts:180) and `Sheet.toggleCheckboxAt` feeds it to `setData` (sheet.ts:3846). `setData` -> `inferInput` treats any value starting with `=` as a formula (input.ts:234, sheet.ts:1033-1034), and `normalizeDataValidationRule` (data-validation.ts:66-102) validates only id/kind/ranges/list/date operands — `checkedValue`/`uncheckedValue` are copied unchecked and unbounded. Vector: a malicious collaborator or a crafted import installs a checkbox rule with `checkedValue: '=HYPERLINK("…","OK")'` (HYPERLINK exists: functions-lookup.ts:869); the next victim click on that checkbox plants the attacker's formula into the victim's own cell — a stored formula-injection primitive driven by rule metadata rather than cell content. The newly added `cell?.f` guard (sheet.ts:3842) prevents overwriting an existing formula but does not prevent creating one. Pre-existing rather than introduced here, and the injector already has cell-write rights in the collaborative model, so privilege gain is limited — hence low confidence. Mitigation: reject/normalize checkbox custom values that begin with `=` (or write them as literals).
searchedFor: Grep 'checkedValue|uncheckedValue' repo-wide (only types.ts, data-validation.ts, tests, docs — no importer or validator sets/validates them)
Read Sheet.setData / inferInput to confirm leading '=' becomes cell.f
Grep 'IMPORTDATA|WEBSERVICE|IMPORTXML|HYPERLINK' in packages/sheets/src for a payload sink

Rules are persisted and re-read through the Yorkie document (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:892-907) and `cloneDataValidationRule` spreads whatever fields exist, so a rule stored with an explicit `null` custom value would behave as a default checkbox for `checkedValueOf` but as a custom checkbox for the new branch. finding.summary: New formula read-only guard checks only `cell?.f`, so spill-ghost cells (array-formula results) still reach `setData` and `toggleCheckboxAt` reports `true` for a write that silently never happens
finding.evidence: Guard added at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3842 tests only `cell.f`. A cell that is a spill ghost of an array formula carries `spillAnchor` + `v` but no `f` (see the ghost-cell contract at sheet.ts:1004: `if (existing?.spillAnchor) return;`). So a checkbox over a spilled formula result passes the new guard, calls `setData` (sheet.ts:3846), which returns early without writing, yet `toggleCheckboxAt` returns `true`. Callers that trust the return — packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:365-367 and packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4853 — re-render believing the state flipped, and the stated invariant "a formula drives the state, the control is read-only" is not enforced for array-formula-driven checkboxes. Fix belongs on the new guard (also check `cell?.spillAnchor`).

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. `toggleCheckboxAt` guards only on `cell?.f` (sheet.ts:3842), while `getCell` returns the raw stored cell (sheet.ts:872-873) and spill-ghost cells are written as `{ v, spillAnchor }` with no `f` (calculator.ts:128). A ghost therefore passes the guard, reaches `setData` (sheet.ts:3846), which returns early without writing (sheet.ts:1004), yet `toggleCheckboxAt` returns `true` — contradicting its documented contract (sheet.ts:3831-3832). The path is reachable: an untoggled checkbox cell has no `v`/`f`, so it does not block a spill under calculator.ts:96, letting an array formula spill into a checkbox-ruled range. Consumers act on the false signal (spreadsheet.ts:365-367, worksheet.ts:4853-4855). I weighed `already-guarded` because sheet.ts:1004 does prevent the actual overwrite (so no data loss), but nothing guards the incorrect return value or enforces the read-only-formula invariant for spill-driven checkboxes, so the presence claim cannot be concretely refuted; the fix belongs on the new guard (also test `cell?.spillAnchor`).
